title: Branded and opaque types for domain safety
hook: TypeScript is structurally typed — two string-typed values are interchangeable even when one is a UserId and the other is an OrderId. Branded types add a phantom compile-time tag so you cannot pass a raw string where a branded UserId is required.

blocks.text: A **branded type** (nominal typing simulation) intersects a base type with a unique phantom property: `type UserId = string & { readonly __brand: 'UserId' }`. Values are still plain strings at runtime — the brand exists only for the type checker. **Opaque types** (via `declare const __brand: unique symbol`) hide the underlying representation — consumers cannot construct the type without a factory function. Use brands for **domain primitives**: UserId, Email, Cents, JWT — preventing swapped-argument bugs.

entries.plainDefinition: Phantom property making structurally identical types incompatible at compile time.
Branded type where constructor is not exported — only factory can create values.
entries.example: declare const Tag: unique symbol; type Opaque = string & { [Tag]: true }

entries.plainDefinition: TS compares shape, not name — brands add fake shape for safety.
entries.example: Two string aliases interchangeable without brand

entries.plainDefinition: Validates and casts raw input to branded type — single creation point.

blocks.text: `deleteUser(orderId)` compiles when both are strings — production disaster. Brands catch it at compile time. C# uses distinct record wrappers or strong-typed IDs (e.g. `record UserId(string Value)`) with real nominal types at runtime. TypeScript brands are zero-cost — no runtime wrapper unless you add validation in the factory. Reddit senior threads pair brands with Zod `.brand()` for runtime + compile-time safety.

blocks.title: Brand at validation boundary
blocks.body: Create UserId only in parseUserId() after regex/UUID check — never cast with as UserId at call sites.

blocks.title: Branding without validation
blocks.body: as UserId everywhere is a lie — brand only helps when creation is centralized.

blocks.title: Serializable brands
blocks.body: JSON.stringify drops phantom fields — brands survive only in TS source, not over wire. Re-parse at boundary.

blocks.text: Alternatives: wrapper class `class UserId { constructor(private readonly value: string) {} }` — nominal at runtime with allocation cost. Zod `z.string().uuid().brand<'UserId'>()` unifies runtime + type. Compare to C# `readonly record struct UserId(string Value)`. Opaque type pattern from type-fest. Senior trap: brands do not survive JSON.parse — re-brand after validation.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying brands exist at runtime. Cannot explain structural vs nominal. as UserId without factory. Not re-parsing after JSON.

interviewTakeaways: Brands add phantom tag: string & { __brand: 'X' } — compile-time only.
Factory function validates then casts — single creation point.
Prevents swapped string arguments — UserId vs OrderId.
60s: Structural typing lets any string substitute. Brand blocks without factory. Zero runtime cost. Re-parse after JSON. C# uses record wrapper for real nominal.
Follow-up: Zod brand or opaque unique symbol pattern.
commonPitfalls: Weak: as UserId at every call site — no safety.
Weak: brand survives JSON — it does not.
Strong: 'unique symbol brand, opaque factory, validate at boundary. Zod brand for runtime+compile.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript Symbol properties can tag objects at runtime — TS brands are compile-time only but solve the same swapped-argument problem.
Brands are the standard workaround for structural typing limits — two string types otherwise interchangeable.
